situation: I want to ask my old manager Diane for advice on moving into product management. Haven't talked to her in 3 years.
reply: Hi Diane, I'll be upfront: I'm reaching out because I'm thinking about moving into product management and you're the first person whose advice I wanted, which feels a bit cheeky after three years. I still use your 'write the press release first' trick on every project. If you had 20 minutes in the next few weeks for a call, I'd be really grateful; if not, no hard feelings at all.
note: Name the ask honestly; a reconnect that hides a favour reads worse when the favour arrives.

situation: 大学室友，毕业后五年没怎么联系了。今天刷到她朋友圈，说在成都开了一家书店。
reply: 好久不见，一晃都五年了。刚看到你在成都开了书店，太像你会做的事了，当年宿舍里就你的书最多。店开得怎么样？不急着回，就是想跟你打个招呼。
note: 不用为断联道歉，用一个具体的原因开头，再问一个好回答的问题。

situation: Me peleé con mi amigo Diego hace un año por una tontería de dinero y no hablamos desde entonces. Quiero escribirle sin reabrir la pelea.
reply: Hola, Diego. Últimamente me he acordado mucho de ti y espero que estés bien. No te escribo por nada en especial. Si algún día te apetece tomar un café, me encantaría.
note: No relitigating the fight; if he replies warmly, suggest a specific day within two messages.
